title: Showing a Sum on the Line

steps.body: A sum drawn on the line tells its whole story: the start mark names the first addend, the jumps name the second, the landing names the answer.
steps.narration: A sum drawn on the line tells its whole story: the start mark names the first addend, the jumps name the second, the landing names the answer.

widget.prompt: Draw 38 + 20 for a reader: two ten-hops from 38.

commonLandings.feedback: A hop of two — the drawn jumps must each be a full ten.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 38, 2 hops land on 58.
widget.successFeedback: 58 — a drawing any classmate could read straight back into the equation.

predict.prompt: In a drawing of 38 + 20, what does the starting mark show?
predict.reveal: The journey begins at the first addend; the answer is where it ENDS.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l show sum.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l show sum.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: The first addend is the start. Which drawing shows 44 + 20?

options.label: Drawing A
options.feedback: Correct — the first addend is the starting mark and the second is the forward journey.

options.label: Drawing B
options.feedback: That drawing reaches the same total but tells the wrong story — 44 is where this sum begins.

options.label: Drawing C
options.feedback: Backward jumps subtract; a plus sign sends every jump to the right.

options.label: Drawing D
options.feedback: Dots alone show positions; a SUM needs the jump that joins them into a journey.

hints: Jump the size the sum names.

steps.body: Communicate a new sum with a route that a classmate can read back into an equation.

widget.prompt: Make a readable route for 29 + 30: take three ten-hops forward from 29.

commonLandings.feedback: That route uses ones. The equation's second addend is three tens.

widget.missFeedback: A reader needs three equal ten-hops. From 29, they land on 59.
widget.successFeedback: 59 — the start, three ten-hops, and landing tell the complete 29 + 30 story.

widget.prompt: 36 + 40 = ? (jumping forward by tens on the line)

commonErrors.feedback: Those jumps were ones — each forward jump here is a whole ten.
One jump too many; count the tens jumps the sum actually asks for.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Walk the line: find the start mark, take the jumps one at a time, and read the mark you land on.
